title: Admin telemetry‑led autofixlets and circuit breakers
creator: Evelyn Chen
description:
Problem: Support teams repeatedly execute ad-hoc remediation scripts for common, observable incidents (OOMs on dedicated pools, model kernel stalls, KV-cache invalidations). These are fragile, often lack telemetry correlation, and can exacerbate incidents when executed at scale.

Proposal: Build a small runtime + console surface for "autofixlets": parameterized, idempotent remediation steps wired to telemetry alerts that can either suggest a human-triggered run or auto-run under strict circuit-breaker conditions. The system pairs each autofixlet with a runtime safety gate (circuit breaker) that enforces rate limits, scoped blast radius, and required approvals. Integrate with existing runbook step registry so autofixlets are discoverable as scheduled recipes or as single-step tasks in the support UI.

Goals: reduce mean time to resolution for common incidents, reduce manual toil, and provide guaranteed safe defaults and observability when automated fixes run. Ensure rollbacks and dry-run mode are first-class.
acceptance_criteria: Autofixlet registry: Operators can register a new autofixlet with metadata (intent, inputs, estimated blast radius, required approval level).
Telemetry binding: Each autofixlet can be attached to one or more alert rules or SLO breaches; bindings are editable via the console.
Circuit-breaker policy: Configurable rate limits, concurrency caps, and per-customer blast radius enforcement are respected before auto-execution.
Dry-run support: Every autofixlet supports a dry-run that simulates actions and returns expected changes without mutating state. Dry-runs are logged and visible in the console.
Observability: Every execution (suggested or automatic) emits structured telemetry (action_id, inputs, outcome, duration, pre/post snapshots) that appears in the ops dashboard.
Rollback: If an autofixlet declares a rollback step, the system can atomically invoke it when an outcome matches failure predicates.
RBAC/Gating: Execution paths respect RBAC and approval flows; auto-executions must be explicitly enabled per-project.
steps: Design data model for autofixlet (metadata, inputs, safety policy, rollback, telemetry schema).
Proto: Implement a lightweight execution runtime inside ops-scheduler that runs sandboxed steps with timeouts and resource caps.
Circuit-breaker infra: Add policy enforcement layer to runtime (rate limit, concurrency, per-customer cap).
Telemetry: Extend op-telemetry ingestion to accept action-correlated traces and link to alert IDs.
Console: Add UI surface to register autofixlets, attach alerts, and configure safety gates.
Dry-run and audit log: Implement dry-run path and append-only execution audit logs surfaced in console.
E2E tests: Create fault-injection tests to validate rollback and circuit-breaker behavior under load.
Docs + runbook: Publish usage guide for SREs and template library of safe autofixlets.
